lines: In the spring of two hundred and eighteen B C, two powers held the western Mediterranean.
Rome, master of Italy. And Carthage, a trading empire stretching from Africa into Spain.
From New Carthage, in Spain, a twenty-nine-year-old general named Hannibal set out to invade Italy by land.
According to the Greek historian Polybius, he crossed the Ebro with about ninety thousand infantry and twelve thousand cavalry.
Many historians think those numbers are inflated.
His route ran north along the coast, over the Pyrenees, across the Rhône,
and into the Alps, by a pass that historians still argue about today.
When he came down into northern Italy, Polybius counts about twenty thousand infantry and six thousand cavalry.
He had lost more than half his army before fighting a single major battle in Italy.
So how did he win anyway?
